outcome: The mathematical question is untouched: no proof, disproof, or bound improvement was found. The only concrete event in the window is a Lean formalization of the conjecture's statement (not a proof) in the google-deepmind/formal-conjectures repository, produced with the help of Claude Opus 4.6, plus a later bug-fix to that formalization's fidelity — neither of which changes what a careful person would write in this bullet.

ai.basis_quote: The formalization was completed with assistance from Claude Opus 4.6.

summary: Nothing has happened to the underlying mathematical question since 26 January 2024. All known betrothed (quasi-amicable) pairs — (48,75), (140,195), (1050,1925), (1575,1648), (2024,2295), (5775,6128), etc. — remain opposite-parity, and it is still open whether a same-parity pair exists; the standing observation that any such pair would have to exceed 10^13 is unchanged and I found no computational search extending that bound. The one concrete event in the window is procedural rather than mathematical: on 2026-02-15, PR #2264 in google-deepmind/formal-conjectures ('feat(Wikipedia): Conjectures about Betrothed Numbers', merged by maintainer mo271) closed issue #2243 ('Do betrothed number pairs with the same parity exist?') by encoding the conjecture as an unproved Lean statement (a benchmark item, not a proof attempt), with the formalization itself produced with the help of Claude Opus 4.6. A later issue (#4998, closed via PR #4999) flagged that the Lean encoding of 'same_parity_betrothed' omitted the constraint m ≠ n, letting quasiperfect numbers (a separate, also-open conjecture) slip through the existential; that issue explicitly states 'the mathematics remains untouched' and both conjectures are still open. I also checked an unrelated arXiv preprint that surfaced in search, 'Formalization of Amicable Numbers Theory' (arXiv 2601.07444, Chen/Tang/Zhan, Jan 2026) — a Lean 4 formalization of classical amicable-number theorems (Thâbit's formula, Euler's rule, the Borho–Hoffmann breeding method) that mentions betrothed numbers only in passing as an extension, again formalizing already-known facts, not advancing the same-parity question. Wikipedia's own article was edited in Jan 2026 (clarifying an OEIS A005276 cross-reference) and March 2026 (math markup formatting only) — no substantive change to the parity claim. Under §6.2, an AI system whose only contribution is formalising a human-authored (Wikipedia-sourced) conjecture statement, with no proof or new mathematics attributed to it, is ai_role none with formalisation_only true — this is exactly that case, not 'assisted', since Claude Opus 4.6 produced no mathematics that appears in any result (there is no result).
competing_reading: One could argue the formalization event itself deserves a `progress` label since a well-known lab (DeepMind's formal-conjectures project) touched this exact problem and it is now a tracked, machine-checkable benchmark item — a structural change in how the problem is pursued even though no mathematics moved. I read `progress` as requiring a bound to move or an instructive incident, neither of which occurred here (the 'incident' was a formalization bug, not an AI mathematical claim that was withdrawn), so I kept status `open`.
what_would_settle_it: A Lean proof or disproof replacing the `sorry` in the formal-conjectures repository's betrothed-numbers file, or a paper/preprint that either exhibits a same-parity betrothed pair or proves none can exist below some bound larger than 10^13.

dead_ends: arXiv 2601.07444 ('Formalization of Amicable Numbers Theory') looked promising from its abstract's mention of 'parity constraint theorems' and betrothed numbers, but on full-text inspection it only formalizes already-known classical results (Thâbit, Euler, Borho-Hoffmann) and makes no new claim about the same-parity question.

DeepMind's May 2026 AlphaProof Nexus result (44/492 OEIS conjectures proved, arXiv 2605.22763) looked like it could include this problem since A005276 is an OEIS sequence, but the paper's extracted text shows no mention of betrothed numbers, quasi-amicable numbers, or A005276, and issue #2243 shows no linked resolution PR from that effort — only the earlier, unrelated formalization PR #2264.

incomplete: I could not access the full PDF/HTML body of arXiv 2605.22763 with complete confidence (extraction returned mostly metadata/structural content), so I cannot be fully certain the DeepMind 44-of-492 OEIS result did not include this conjecture under a different framing. However, issue #2243 on GitHub — the direct locus where such a resolution would be recorded — shows no such resolution, only the unrelated 2026-02-15 formalization PR, which I weight as the stronger signal.
